one_line_contribution: A 2x2 provenance crossover in ALFWorld in which a GEPA-optimized instruction and a distilled experience bank are each built from the same training episodes but labelled by which three of the six task types produced them, so that the amount of a memory bank's task-specific value already absorbed by the instruction can be read off the instruction-provenance x bank-provenance interaction at matched test type, with an information-free best-of-w sampling ladder used to subtract the headroom compression that the accuracy gap between the two instructions would produce mechanically.
closest_prior_work: Two, jointly. (a) MIPROv2 (2406.11695): its instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint ablation is exactly the two-container question, and its published finding that the split is task-dependent already supplies the qualitative answer this proposal seeks; what the proposal adds over it is retrieval, distillation, token matching and the provenance labelling, which is a sharper instrument for a question whose direction is known. (b) EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) as the proposal itself reports it: ReasoningBank +3.6 vs GEPA +1.2 on shared 528/267 trajectories on Qwen3.5-27B is already the headline that an optimizer on the same episodes gets roughly what the bank gets. The proposal is candid that this sentence is in the literature and cites it as motivation. Neither work manipulates provenance or puts an optimizer and a bank in the same context, so novelty is not extinguished, but what remains is a measurement refinement of an accepted qualitative claim, not a new phenomenon. Experience Distillation (2607.21051) is a third threat on the quantity itself: retains >=64.8% of an in-context gain in a second container is the same retention-ratio result with weights rather than an instruction as the rival container.
strongest_objection: The confirmatory threshold is arithmetically incompatible with the gate that licenses it. Delta_abs = [Inner(I_oth) - Inner(I_own)] - ladder correction, and the ladder correction is positive by the proposal's own argument (I_own sits above I_oth in level, so compression makes D positive mechanically). If Inner(I_own) >= 0, which is what the absorption hypothesis rather than the interference hypothesis predicts, then Delta_abs <= Inner(I_oth) - correction. G3 only requires the relevance advantage to clear 4pt with a lower CI of 1pt, and Inner(I_oth) is measured at an optimized instruction, i.e. at a level at or above I0 where compression is if anything worse. So a Delta_abs of 5pt requires the on-type bank's advantage to be essentially annihilated and then some at I_own, while the design admits itself into the confirmatory stage on a 4pt advantage. Under the gate's own floor the effect the study claims to be powered for cannot occur, and a real, substantial partial absorption of, say, 40% of a 5pt advantage is 2pt, far below both the 5pt threshold and the 4.6-4.8pt MDE, and would be reported as inconclusive. The modal realized outcome of this design is therefore a bounded null on the primary, and the paper falls back on secondary endpoints that are much closer to what EvoAgentBench and MIPROv2 already show. Two supporting design gaps sharpen this. First, there is no gate on the instruction-provenance main effect (cells 8 vs 9), even though the proposal correctly states that an instruction that learned nothing type-specific cannot have absorbed anything type-specific; GEPA on ALFWorld plausibly buys generic scaffolding (action syntax, receptacle enumeration, re-prompt discipline) that transfers across all six types, in which case the square is guaranteed null before it is run, and G0-G5 will not catch it. Second, ladder B, which Risk Factor 3 names as the direct test of the one-dimensionality assumption the entire headroom correction rests on, is third on the Tier-0 contingency cut list, ahead of reducing optimizer seeds and ahead of reducing n; the pre-registered degradation path deletes the validation of the primary statistic while keeping the statistic.
what_would_fix_it: Re-derive the gate from the endpoint instead of setting them independently. G3 should require a dev relevance advantage of roughly 10-12pt, not 4pt, or the primary should be restated as an absorbed fraction 1 - Inner(I_own)/Inner(I_oth) with a threshold on the ratio and the design powered for the ratio's delta-method CI, which is currently only a descriptive quantity. Add a gate on the instruction-provenance main effect, acc(I_own x M0) - acc(I_oth x M0) > 0 with a lower CI above zero on S_dev2, and branch to the level-based endpoint if it fails, since the square is uninterpretable without it. Move ladder B off the cut list and cut n or the third optimizer seed instead. Decompose Inner(I) into its help component acc(I x B_own) - acc(I x M0) and its harm component acc(I x M0) - acc(I x B_oth) using cells 8 and 9, and pre-register that absorption requires the help component to shrink: as written, a shrinking Inner at I_own is equally consistent with the optimized instruction making the agent more robust to irrelevant injected text, which is distractor-robustness rather than content transfer, and the fix/break 2/3 rule does not separate the two. Finally, add a direct content check the design currently lacks entirely: a textual overlap or ablation analysis showing that I_own actually contains the procedures that B_own's items encode. The claim in the title is about content moving between containers, and the whole plan tests only a behavioral interaction.
missing_baseline: I_all: an instruction optimized on the union of both type sets, crossed with {M0, B_own, B_oth} on S_test. Every cell of the square uses an instruction optimized on only half the task space, which is a configuration no practitioner would deploy, yet predictions 5 and 6 are stated as the practitioner's number and as a deployment recommendation to compile once and drop retrieval. I1_all appears only in cell 20, at Tier 1, with 2 seeds on the 274-game official splits, which is badly underpowered for the 3pt bounds those predictions use and is cuttable. A reviewer will say the deployment claim is made in a condition never measured at power. Secondary omission with the same character: the long-context dump baselines M_all and R_raw are Tier 1, although the proposal itself cites EvoMemBench for long-context baselines remaining highly competitive against 15 memory methods, and AutoMEM for a flat-file harness beating eight of them; if raw dumping matches the bank, the container framing loses its second container before absorption is even at issue.
preprint_collision: Process is well above what proposals in this area usually show: two dated scans, 15 HuggingFace queries over 244 papers, by-id abstract verification for 54 IDs, a committed litscan table with the rule that no cited ID is absent from it, EvoAgentBench read from the PDF with a committed SHA256, and a self-correction of a web snippet that had misreported ReasoningBank's Qwen gain as +7 against the PDF's +3.6, plus reinstatement of five IDs wrongly retracted in v2. I credit that. But the check does not establish novelty, by the proposal's own accounting. The only thing claimed as new is the use of the provenance crossover as the identification of container substitution, and obligation (2), the targeted search of the prompt-optimization, contamination and data-attribution literatures for held-out-episode and data-provenance crossovers, has never been run from this node. An unsearched claim is a weakness: crossover designs of exactly this shape are routine in data attribution and in contamination auditing, and the odds that no 2026 preprint has applied one to a prompt optimizer or a memory bank are not low. Obligation (1), the unopened appendix of 2608.14036, is acknowledged as the collision that would gut prediction 6, and obligation (3), cross-task-type transfer of procedural memory in the embodied-agent literature, targets precisely the type-set manipulation the instrument is built on. Also material: arXiv is unreachable from the node, so every load-bearing 2026 ID rests on web-search snippets through a single channel. I can independently confirm only the pre-2026 anchors, and those are accurate as characterized (ExpeL 2308.10144, A-MEM 2502.12110, Memp 2508.06433, GEPA 2507.19457 with its >10% over MIPROv2 and ~35x rollout claim, MIPROv2 2406.11695, ReasoningBank 2509.25140), which is a real credibility signal; the 2026 IDs, including MemHarness 2607.28272 whose 70.1/76.4/85.2 numbers carry the premise that ALFWorld memory effects are 5-15 points, I cannot verify and neither, on one channel, can the authors. No preprint I know of makes this exact claim, so I do not find a hard collision; I find a novelty claim that the submission itself marks conditional on searches not yet performed, and that is how I have scored it.
